rationale: The worst path touches an IO port. IO delays are 20% of the period, so IO slack scales as 0.8T. Using the source delays (IO K≈4.20 ns, reg-to-reg ≈5.21 ns), R1=5.85 gives IO slack ≈+0.48 ns and reg-to-reg ≈+0.64 ns, so C0 overstates the clock the design needs. Synthesis should stay essentially unchanged because the ABC area script sees tt delays well below either target. Only timing-driven placement/CTS noise (~0.1 ns) differs, and post-CTS repair (0.283 ns margin) should not trigger. Hold is reg-to-reg, does not depend on the clock and is repaired to ~0.1 ns; IO hold margins stay large. DRC and DRV were clean at 28% utilisation. The remaining risk is hold, DRC or flow noise. C1 ≈ max(0.2·R1+4.20, 5.21)+noise ≈5.39, so slope ≈0.19. Chain: R2≈5.40 (base slack +0.12, repair lifts it to ~+0.24), then R3≈5.20 (needs a small resizer gain), then R4≈5.0 (marginal). Median kept clock ≈5.20.
